Alongside macOS 26.6, Apple has also released macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, which include important bug fixes. Here are the details.

macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 are finally officially released

After testing through as many as seven Release Candidates, Apple has finally officially released macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8.

The version numbers of the official releases are the same as last week's Release Candidates:

  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 (23J620)
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 (24G824)

Apple's release notes only indicate that these two updates provide "important security fixes" and recommend that all users still running macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia install them.

In recent weeks, Apple has rolled out multiple security fixes for older system versions, many of which patch WebKit vulnerabilities that could lead to user data leaks. Therefore, if you are still using macOS Sonoma or macOS Sequoia, it is recommended to install these updates as soon as possible.

Update: Apple has published the complete security content for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, detailing over 138 different vulnerabilities across the two systems combined.

Are you still using macOS Sonoma or macOS Sequoia? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
